record.distance_note: The existing 22nd St Caltrain station (Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St, Dogpatch) sits roughly 400-450m from both Pier 70's and Potrero Power Station's tracked boundaries -- grouped here under Pier 70 as the closer, better-established Dogpatch association.

record.summary: An accessibility retrofit of the existing, below-grade 22nd Street Caltrain station -- the only regular-service Caltrain station without wheelchair access. The project adds ramps to both platforms plus wayfinding and safety improvements. The design phase is funded and scheduled, not shown as started: the SFCTA Board approved $1.3 million for it in April 2026 and Caltrain expects to complete design by summer 2027. Sources disagree on when the station would open for use: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 2026 post and presentation), December 2029 (the project description in SFCTA's April 14 packet) and "the end of 2029" (The Voice of San Francisco, October 2026), all subject to funding. In September 2026 the Federal Transit Administration announced a $14.1 million All Stations Accessibility Program award to Caltrain's board for the station (Trains.com, September 16, 2026). Sponsored by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) with SFCTA (Prop L) and FTA funding.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box over the existing station's real location, not a traced footprint of the platforms or the planned ramps themselves (one ~305ft ramp on the northbound platform, one ~465ft ramp on the southbound platform, per the project's own design description).
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for the existing 22nd St Caltrain station or its below-grade platforms (active rail right-of-way, the same reasoning already documented for the nearby 4th & King Station in the Mission Bay railyards record -- confirmed here too: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset has no parcel at this location). No Caltrain/Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available, so this is a coarse locational box near the real DataSF street-centerline address range for 22nd St at Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St (DataSF's official street centerlines), where the existing below-grade station sits.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Active Caltrain rail right-of-way; not on the Assessor's secured roll, the same situation as the existing 4th & King Street Station (mapped in Pier & Point's Mission Bay railyards record).
notes.regulatory_context: The Caltrain 22nd Street Station is the railroad's only regular-service station that is not wheelchair accessible: its platforms sit about 25 ft below street level, reachable only by stairs. Sponsor: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain); funded in part through SFCTA's Prop L. Total project cost per SFCTA's April 2026 Board Packet: $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L, approved by the SFCTA Board 2026-04-14 and given final approval 2026-04-28; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). The FTA's 'All Stations Accessibility Program' separately awarded the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board $14.1 million for this project's ADA improvements, announced in September 2026 (the day is not given by the sources read) -- matching almost exactly the funding gap SFCTA's own April 2026 plan had left as 'Planned TBD'.

facts.value: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), with funding from SFCTA (Prop L) and the FTA

One ramp on the northbound platform (about 305 ft long, 6.5% slope) and one on the southbound platform (about 465 ft long, 6.1% slope), plus tactile strips, lighting and signage. Platforms sit about 25 ft below street grade, currently reachable only by stairs.

open_questions: This record's placement under Pier 70 rather than Potrero Power Station reflects a roughly equal real-world distance (about 400-450m to each tracked boundary) plus the station's more established association with the Dogpatch/Pier 70 corridor in transit planning -- not a precise geometry test against a real station footprint (no Assessor parcel or site-plan figure exists to test against; the map shape is a coarse placeholder box; see its accuracy note).

No source says design work has begun or how far along it is. SFCTA's April 14, 2026 packet schedules design from April 2026 to September 2027 ("Review 30% design and other documentation: 7/1/26 – 8/1/26"; geotechnical report "anticipated October 2026") and gives "Start Construction" as April-June 2028, but that is a plan written before the work, and no source dated after the planned start reports progress.

When the station would open for use is given three ways: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post and its April 14 presentation), December 2029 (the project description in SFCTA's April 14 packet) and the end of 2029 (The Voice of San Francisco, October 6, 2026). The packet's own allocation form lists "Open for Use" in April-June 2029 and "Project Completion (means last eligible expenditure)" in July-September 2029. All are subject to funding, which was not secured when the dates were written; the record shows 2029 only.
